patterns.usage_note: が marks the subject of a clause and presents it as new information rather than a known topic, so it is used when the whole sentence is the news (雨が降ってきた) or when the subject answers a question (私が行きます). Its siblings are the が marking what a stative predicate is about (日本語が分かる) and the clause-linking が meaning but (高いが買った). Inside a noun-modifying clause it may be replaced by の (私が読んだ本 / 私の読んだ本).

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の家[いえ]から焼[や]きたてのパンの匂[にお]いがする。
examples.english: The smell of fresh-baked bread is drifting over from next door.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]がピアノのコンクールで優勝[ゆうしょう]した。
examples.english: My little sister won the piano competition.

examples.ruby: 教室[きょうしつ]の電気[でんき]がまだ消[き]えていない。
examples.english: The lights in the classroom still aren't off.

glosses: marks the subject of a noun-modifying clause
patterns.usage_note: Marks the subject inside a noun-modifying or nominalized clause, standing where が would otherwise stand: 父の作った料理, 日の暮れるのが早い. Two sibling entries take the other jobs of this の: turning a clause into a noun (走るのが速い) and listing off what someone is fussing about (行くの行かないのと騒ぐ). It is blocked when the modifying clause carries its own を-object, and speakers typically avoid it when the clause is long or already contains another の.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]の作[つく]った味噌汁[みそしる]は少[すこ]し塩辛[しおから]い。
examples.english: The miso soup my father made is a little on the salty side.

examples.ruby: 日[ひ]の暮[く]れるのが日[ひ]に日[ひ]に早[はや]くなる。
examples.english: The sun is going down a little earlier with each passing day.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]の担当[たんとう]する授業[じゅぎょう]はいつも満員[まんいん]だ。
examples.english: The classes that professor teaches are always packed.

patterns.usage_note: Marks the person a capacity, judgment or burden rests with, the experiencer subject that pairs with potential forms, 分かる, and 無理/大変-type predicates (俺には分からない, 素人には無理だ). Sibling lanes take the person told something (親に言う), an attitude aimed at someone (子供に優しい), and the source something comes from (親方に教わる). にゃ has は built into it, so it readily reads as contrast: someone else might manage it.

examples.ruby: 俺[おれ]にゃそんな難[むずか]しい話[はなし]は分[わ]からない。
examples.english: That kind of complicated talk is over my head.

examples.ruby: 六歳[ろくさい]の弟[おとうと]にゃ、この自転車[じてんしゃ]は大[おお]きすぎる。
examples.english: This bike is too big for my six-year-old brother.

examples.ruby: 素人[しろうと]にゃこの機械[きかい]の修理[しゅうり]は無理[むり]だ。
examples.english: Fixing this machine is beyond an amateur.
